fact: The Office of the Chief Procurement Officer launched the e-Tender Publication portal on 1 April 2015 as a single platform for publishing national, provincial and (from 1 July 2015) municipal tenders and award notices.

The OECD, World Bank and AfDB MAPS assessment says South Africa's organs of state publish tenders on the eTenders e-procurement system, with 73% of registered organs of state publishing tenders in financial year 2023-2024.
The MAPS assessment gives eTenders use figures for 2023-2024: 73% of registered organs of state published tenders, 12% uploaded procurement plans and 3% published contract notices.

National Treasury's SCM Instruction 09 of 2022/23 requires departments, constitutional institutions and Schedule 2 and 3 public entities to publish open competitive bids, amendments, cancellations and awards on the e-Tender Portal from 1 November 2022.
National Treasury's OCPO deck says the eTenders system handles tender publication, online bid submission (eSubmission), online bid evaluations and publication of awards, used by 892 organs of state.

National Treasury's OCPO deck says eTenders covers procurement planning, tender publication, online bid submission and evaluation, awards data and contract lifecycle management for 892 organs of state.
National Treasury's OCPO deck gives eTenders averages of 3,300 tenders and 1,800 awards a month.

A National Treasury spokesperson told Business Day the current system is still largely paper based and an electronic government procurement system is being developed, to be introduced in phases under the Public Procurement Act 2024.
